testCase.name: [local] S06 Nursing Home visit number keeps rising with admission age and visits, including past the 'last two visits' window

descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-92579 AC 3 + AC 4 · “The hospital day / visit number advances each calendar day (server time) and never stays frozen”. Mixed: stated part — visit number shown and rising with visits; our part — N5 still above N4 although only two of its visits are retained (3.6 window) (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Bug B23 · S1 · known

Patient cards are missing fields: age shows '76y' not '76F', Hospital cards have no hospital day, Nursing Home cards no visit number

Tickets: TFA-92579 AC3–4 ready for qa · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: dev + local

Note: Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579): the backend stores sex = F, yet the card shows '76y'; the Nursing Home diagnosis cells of TC-01/S03 and S26 are B28's root cause, so they need no Q4.

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S03, TC-01/S05, TC-01/S26, TC-01/S07

Approach · TC-01 Patient Chart Card · S06 Nursing Home visit number keeps rising with admission age and visits, including past the 'last two visits' window

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U5 The card shows the hospital day (Hospital) or the visit number (Nursing Home). (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 3)
  • U6 The day/visit number advances each calendar day by server time and never stays frozen; a device with a wrong clock or time zone shows the same number. (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 4; UAT 3.8)
  • U8 With multiple patients loaded, everything above holds in both Hospital and Nursing Home. (UAT TC-01; UAT 3.3)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given seededCensus N1 (admitted today, 0 prior visits), N3 (−3 d, 1 prior), N4 (−7 d, 2 prior), N5 (−14 d, 4 prior on distinct days; 3.6 keeps only the last two)

When Read each resident's visit number on the card (Today's Visits and All Residents)

Then N1 shows the first value; N1 < N3 < N4 < N5; N5 is above N4 even though only two of its visits are retained

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Q3-independent: N1 = the first value ('Visit 1' format per Q3) and strictly N1 < N3 < N4 < N5. A number counted from retained visits caps at 3 under 3.6 and fails N5 > N4; a frozen number fails the ordering. The comparison needs numbers read per card, so it lives in the card-scoped spec (S26); oracle.mjs only matches substrings. …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S06 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: Known product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92579 ready for qa

Nursing Home resident cards show no visit number at all, so a resident on a fifth visit looks the same as one admitted today.

Evidence: newspec-a lane (N1/N3/N4/N5 seeded) plus the datasets lane. This is the visit-number half of dev report §2 #5 (C2, 'no hospital day / visit number', U27). The format is still open (Q3), but it does not matter because no number is shown.

Folded in: local datasets TC-01/S06 (same failure, folded into this result)
